name: Invoice to cash agent
summary: Match synthetic invoices and bank lines, retain exceptions, and prepare reminders that require approval.
problem: Partial payments, duplicate bank lines and missing references make an invoice balance hard to trust. A reminder also needs to survive worker restarts without being delivered twice.
architecture: Import and reconcile
PostgreSQL stores invoices, bank lines and allocations. Integer minor units preserve balances; ambiguous references go to review.
Persist the workflow
Day-14 reminder jobs and completed steps remain in the database. A polling worker resumes pending work after restart.
Prepare and review
A mock or Claude provider drafts text. Customer history adds an escalation record. A trusted operator approves the current balance and draft.
Dispatch atomically
A transactional demonstration mailbox shares its commit with the delivery checkpoint. Retries cannot create another mailbox entry.
tradeoffs: Reconciliation locks all invoices in a stable order. This is easy to inspect and test, but limits throughput.
The transactional mailbox proves local delivery idempotency. A real email transport would need its own durable idempotency contract.
limits: No bank integration, currency conversion, public authentication or real email delivery.
The Claude adapter is implemented but live model quality was not measured.
Approval uses a trusted local operator identity. This is a CLI showcase.
evaluation: Both native process-kill tests passed: reconciliation and reminder delivery rolled back and resumed without duplicate delivery.
demoOutput:
All data synthetic. Transport: transactional demo mailbox.
Invoice 10000 USD minor units. Partial payment 4000. Remaining: 6000
Dry run: dry-run
Approved delivery: delivered
Retry: delivered
Mailbox records: 1
Persisted steps: [
  { job: 'reminder:demo-invoice', name: 'delivered' },
  { job: 'reminder:demo-invoice', name: 'drafted' },
  { job: 'reminder:demo-invoice', name: 'escalated' }
]

name: Support resolution agent
summary: Resolve synthetic store tickets with guarded refund, address-change and reschedule tools.
problem: A helpful reply does not resolve a ticket when the store record still needs an action. Tool execution must check ownership, policy and limits, and recover safely when a response is lost.
architecture: Propose an intent
A mock or Claude provider proposes a typed action from untrusted ticket text. It cannot choose the authenticated principal or grant permission.
Enforce store guards
The PostgreSQL-backed mock store checks the ticket owner, order state, return window, refund cap and exact action shape.
Commit once
The store mutation, idempotency ledger and success audit share one transaction. A lost response can be retried without repeating the action.
Escalate and replay
Ambiguity and denied or failed actions are audited and escalated. A replay harness compares ticket outcomes and store state with independent fixture labels.
tradeoffs: Only one automatic refund is allowed per order. A follow-up partial refund goes to a person.
The store API is an in-process boundary with persistent idempotency, rather than a real retailer integration.
limits: The replay contains 16 policy templates with 10 synthetic identities each. It is a regression fixture set.
Replay results use the deterministic mock provider, not Claude. They do not establish production resolution rates.
Caller identity is trusted local context; no public identity server is included.
evaluation: Synthetic replay: 160 tickets, 50 resolved (31.25%), 110 escalated (68.75%), and zero wrong-action, state or label mismatches.

name: Permission aware knowledge search
summary: Apply current source permissions inside the pgvector query before returning document chunks.
problem: A search result can disclose restricted content even if its source link is hidden later. Retrieval needs to enforce source access before ranking and before a model receives context.
architecture: Normalize mock sources
Drive, Slack and Notion-style connectors store source nodes, folder relationships, user/group grants and revocable link capabilities.
Separate content and access
Versioned content chunks have local hash embeddings. Source ACLs and group membership remain live metadata, separate from the index.
Filter inside SQL
A recursive ancestry and ACL predicate runs inside PostgreSQL before pgvector ranking and LIMIT. Revoked, deleted and stale content is excluded.
Answer from permitted chunks
Only retrieved chunks reach the answer provider. A user with no accessible evidence gets an empty result without a model invocation.
tradeoffs: The query predicate is the authorization boundary. This is not RLS protection against callers with direct database credentials.
64-dimensional hash vectors are a small lexical baseline with collisions, not production semantic embeddings.
limits: Mock source-access changes are synchronous. Real connector event delays and permission semantics are outside this implementation.
Revocation cannot retract context already sent to a model.
The quality evaluation has five synthetic topical queries. Live Claude answer quality remains unmeasured.
evaluation: Leak suite: 1,728 synthetic user/query pairs across access changes, zero unauthorized chunks. Five-query retrieval evaluation: recall@3 1.0 and MRR 1.0.

name: Sales call to CRM sync
summary: Turn synthetic transcripts into grounded CRM diffs and follow-up drafts, with approval required for every write.
problem: Calls contain multiple speakers, missing facts and contradictory budgets or dates. A CRM update needs traceable evidence and review of the exact change to an existing record.
architecture: Extract with provenance
A mock or Claude provider proposes supported fields with verbatim quotes and speaker labels. Field-specific checks reject unsupported evidence.
Merge all chunks
Long transcripts are processed in chunks. Overlap is merged by source statement, while separate conflicting statements remain flagged.
Show the exact diff
PostgreSQL stores the before/after proposal, evidence, ambiguity flags and base CRM version. Missing fields preserve existing values.
Approve and apply
The trusted operator approves a canonical diff hash. An optimistic version check, CRM write and audit commit atomically; repeated calls or applies reuse checkpoints.
tradeoffs: Grounding deliberately uses a limited English/Urdu phrase set. Unsupported language or values require review.
Next week means the next Monday in the call timezone and is flagged as an interpretation.
limits: The CRM is a PostgreSQL-backed mock, with no real CRM writes or follow-up messages.
Speaker labels must already be present; there is no audio transcription or diarization.
Transcripts are limited to one million UTF-16 code units. Live Claude quality is unmeasured.
evaluation: Tests cover separate speakers, shared-company contacts, distant conflicts in a 4,000-line transcript, stale approvals, lost work and repeated applies.
